what: The live observe-only cognition_shadow bridge op, driven over real Hermes traffic.
not_a_replay: This ran `python -u -m z0int.bridge.worker` and sent real cognition_shadow ops. It is the actual lane, not a re-analysis of a log.

boundary_verified.note: the lane never returned an executable action across all 40 decisions

finding: on the same 40 real decisions and the same 5-action legal set, hammer3b collapsed to `read` 40/40 while nanojev spread across read 20 / skill_view 13 / web_search 6. hammer3b is also 7x slower here (264 ms vs 38 ms p50).
nanojev_note: NanoJev could NOT be shadowed here: the lane resolves models through ~/.z0int/config/serving.json, which lists only llama.cpp-supervised models, and nanojev_06b is an in-process DecisionBackend rather than a served model. The lane recorded that failure correctly (parse_error, abstained=true) rather than silently skipping. To shadow NanoJev the lane needs a DecisionBackend resolution path, not a serving entry.

resolution_fix.problem: the lane resolved models only through ~/.z0int/config/serving.json, which lists llama.cpp-supervised models; nanojev_06b is an in-process DecisionBackend, so the most promising cheap path found was the one path the lane could not watch
resolution_fix.fix: DecisionBackendShadow adapter + opt-in fallback to the z0int DecisionBackend registry, enabled by Z0INT_COGNITION_SHADOW_DECISION_BACKENDS=1. Off by default so existing shadow callers keep the served-model path.
resolution_fix.verified: nanojev shadowed 40/40 real decisions with 1 recorded error, no crash
